assumptions.condition: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).

novel.justification: A shared laboratory pipeline, record-linkage platform, or policy module can preserve the entire latent response block for a confounded district across sites. This is deliberately stronger than ordinary vertex-level selection-diagram invariance because Layer-3 laws depend on cross-world coupling inside the district.

assumptions.condition: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).

novel.justification: Site changes often act on an entire confounded measurement or policy block. Whole-district selection permits arbitrary changes inside that block while ruling out an unsupported splice of cross-world dependence across only part of it.

assumptions.condition:
For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), descriptor \(a\) declares a finite counterfactual tuple \(T_a\), a finite output alphabet \(\mathcal Y_a\), and a deterministic map \(f_a\) into \(\mathcal Y_a\), and
\[
P_a^s=(f_a)_\#\mathcal L_{M^s}(T_a),
\]
where an unpostprocessed descriptor has the identity output map.
For every \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the bidirected subgraph induced by \(D\) is complete.

For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), all mechanisms on \(D\) are generated by one finite latent variable \(U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\), where \(\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\) contains the deterministic response maps at every parent configuration: if \(U_D^s=\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\), then the structural equation of each \(V\in D\) reads the component \(f_V\); the variables \((U_D^s:D\in\mathcal D(G))\) are mutually independent.

definitions.name: District-closed finite transport class
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})=\{\mathbf M=(M^s:s\in\mathcal S):\mathbf M\text{ is recursively compatible, district-factorized, district-kernel invariant, and district-closed}\}.\]

definitions.name: Typed-menu compatibility fiber
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]

definitions.name: Canonical district response profile
definitions.construction: For every \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), set \(\Omega_D=\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\), the finite set of all tuples \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) of deterministic response maps at every parent configuration allowed by \(G\) and \(\mathcal X\).  For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\) is the joint law of the response maps induced by \(M^s\).  The carrier is query independent and includes every configuration needed by any target, menu, deterministic postprocessor, or later acquired regime.

definitions.name: Certified typed extraction judgment
definitions.construction:
For \(P_a^s\in\Delta(\mathcal Y_a)\), write
\[
\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)
\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)
\]
exactly when the finite extraction calculus constructs, for every retained \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), a numerator event \(A_{h,c}\), a context event \(H_h\), derivations
\[
\delta_N:A_{h,c}\Downarrow N_{s,a,D,h,c},
\qquad
\delta_H:H_h\Downarrow H_{s,a,D,h},
\]
two accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) traces, the rows those traces construct,
\[
r_{s,a,D,h,c}=\operatorname{row}_D(A_{h,c}),
\qquad
v_{s,a,D,h}=\operatorname{row}_D(H_h),
\]
and an independently checkable certificate \(\pi_h\) that \(H_{s,a,D,h}>0\) on the declared fiber.  The returned kernel entry is the typed expression
\[
K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=
\operatorname{Quot}(N_{s,a,D,h,c},H_{s,a,D,h},\pi_h).
\]
The record \(\kappa\) contains only the event and expression derivations, locality tables, constructed rows, and positivity certificates.  It contains neither \(N=r^{\mathsf T}q\), nor \(H=v^{\mathsf T}q\), nor any equivalent semantic equality.  An unavailable cell, undefined fixing, rejected locality table, or uncertified denominator has no successful judgment and creates no row-eligibility record.

definitions.name: Context-indexed extracted-cell incidence row
definitions.construction:
For every successful row-eligibility record define the separate numerator and context rows
\[
\begin{split}
r_{s,a,D,h,c}(\omega_D)
&=\mathbf 1\{A_{h,c}\text{ has the common value certified by }
\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\},\\
v_{s,a,D,h}(\omega_D)
&=\mathbf 1\{H_h\text{ has the common value certified by }
\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\},
\end{split}
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D.
\]
For a complete supplied output cell \(C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\), an accepting locality trace similarly constructs
\[
r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y}=\operatorname{row}_D(C_{a,y}).
\]
The quotient \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\) is not an incidence row.

definitions.name: District row face and global projections
definitions.construction:
Define the district row face and its forced-zero coordinates by
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\Omega_D}:A_Dq=m_D\},
\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
Define the broad and saturated global district projections by
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\},
\qquad
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]

definitions.name: Common-evidence arm row system
definitions.construction:
For a fixed district \(D\), a total record \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) consists of: a finite nonempty arm set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\); for every \(\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), an accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(B_\rho\cap E)\) trace and its constructed row \(n_{\rho,D}\); one accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(E)\) trace and its constructed row \(d_D\); a rational or real-algebraic number \(\varepsilon_D>0\); and an exact certificate that
\[
d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D
\qquad\text{for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Only from such a record define, for \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\),
\[
Q_\rho(q)=\frac{n_{\rho,D}^{\mathsf T}q}{d_D^{\mathsf T}q},
\qquad
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}.
\]
Separately, for any target cell \(C\), an accepting \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(C)\) trace constructs the generic target row \(b_D=\operatorname{row}_D(C)\).  If a required locality trace rejects, the corresponding row, comparison, or target value is undefined rather than silently assigned a row.

definitions.name: Sharp transported dominance margin
definitions.construction:
Given a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record and \(\rho,\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), define
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)
=\min_{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q,
\qquad
\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)
=\max_{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q.
\]
The definitions are made only when the checked record exists; its positivity certificate makes every associated conditional comparison well defined on the face.

definitions.name: Menu-dual dominance certificate
definitions.construction:
Given a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record, \(\rho,\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\), and \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), a menu-dual dominance certificate at level \(\gamma\) is a vector \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}\) satisfying
\[
A_D^{\mathsf T}\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}
\leq g_{\rho,\sigma,D}
\quad\text{coordinatewise},
\qquad
m_D^{\mathsf T}\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\geq\gamma.
\]
It is not defined in the absence of the total locality and common-evidence record.

definitions.name: One-cell Layer-3 sign-regime frontier
definitions.construction:
Given a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record and a realizable additional complete Layer-3 output-cell row \(r_D^\dagger\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\), define
\[
I_D=\{(r_D^\dagger)^{\mathsf T}q:q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
For \(p\in I_D\), define
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)
=\min_{\substack{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\\
(r_D^\dagger)^{\mathsf T}q=p}}
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^{\mathsf T}q,
\qquad
\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+
=\{p\in I_D:\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)>0\}.
\]
Every object is defined only from the checked arm rows and their common strictly positive evidence row.

definitions.name: Finite ex-post regime-block acquisition problem
definitions.construction:
Fix a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record.  Each \(e\in\mathcal U\) is a realizable finite block of typed descriptors, possibly with deterministic finite postprocessing.  Acquiring \(e\) reveals the complete finite law of every declared output, including every normalization-dependent complementary cell, equivalently a dependent row-value block \((R_e,p_e)\), at cost \(c_e>0\).  Require joint realizability of the whole experiment menu:
\[
\mathcal K_{\mathcal U}
=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal U\}
\ne\varnothing.
\]
For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define
\[
\mathcal K_S
=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\}.
\]
The checked lower bound \(d_D^{\mathsf T}q\geq\varepsilon_D>0\) persists on every subface.  Hence every local subset is uniformly positive before acquisition, no subset-specific evidence screen is needed, and one may define the local row-face possibly optimal set by
\[
\operatorname{PO}(S)
=\left\{\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}:
\exists q\in\mathcal K_S\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ 
(n_{\rho,D}-n_{\sigma,D})^{\mathsf T}q\geq0\right\}.
\]
Finally set
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),
\qquad
f(S)=|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|-|\operatorname{PO}(S)|,
\]
and define the local ex-post acquisition problem by
\[
\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}.
\]
This construction is the computationally cheap district row-face layer and is the uniformly-positive special case of subset-screened global acquisition.  It does not declare \(\mathcal K_S\) to be the exact projection of the broad multi-district compatibility fiber: that equality requires the separately stated augmented focal-saturation and baseline-averaged separation hypotheses.

definitions.name: Complete binary acquisition and strictness instance
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\) have binary \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\) and isolated binary \(Z\), target \(\star\), source \(s\), and \(\Delta_s=\{Z\}\), so \(D=\{Y\}\) is invariant.  Order
\[
\Omega_D=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}
\]
for \((Y_0,Y_1)\), and set
\[
A_D=\begin{bmatrix}
1&1&1&1\\0&0&1&1\\0&1&0&1
\end{bmatrix},
\qquad m_D=(1,1/2,1/2)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=
\{q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p):0\leq p\leq1/2\},
\qquad Z_D(m_D)=\varnothing.
\]
Take \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\), \(E=\top\),
\[
B_\rho=\{Y_0\ne Y_1\},
\qquad B_\sigma=\{Y_1=1\}.
\]
The exhaustive locality tables construct
\[
n_{\rho,D}=(0,1,1,0),\quad
n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1),\quad
d_D=(1,1,1,1),
\]
and \(\varepsilon_D=1\) with the exact identity \(d_D^{\mathsf T}q=1\) on the face; these data form \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\).  Hence
\[
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=(0,0,-1,1).
\]
Let \(\mathcal U=\{e^\dagger\}\), \(c_{e^\dagger}=1\), and let \(e^\dagger\) return the Boolean output
\[
f^\dagger(Y_0,Y_1)=\mathbf 1\{(Y_0,Y_1)=(1,1)\}.
\]
The complete source output law has \(P_{e^\dagger}^s(1)=3/8\) and \(P_{e^\dagger}^s(0)=5/8\).  Its output-one row is
\[
r_D^\dagger=(0,0,0,1),
\]
the output-zero row is its normalization-dependent complement, and \(\mathcal K_{\mathcal U}=\{q(3/8)\}\ne\varnothing\).  Finally set \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\).

definitions.name: Allowed rational functional
definitions.construction: The algebra \(\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) is generated by rational constants and the directly supplied complete output-cell probabilities \(P_a^s(y)\), including deterministic-pushforward output cells, under finite sums, differences, products, and marginalization sums.  It contains a quotient \(F/H\) only together with an independently checked certificate that \(H\ne0\) on the relevant compatibility fiber; a conditional causal output requires the stronger stored certificate \(H>0\) throughout that fiber.  A quantifier-free semialgebraic range or endpoint description returned by the canonical quantifier-elimination fallback is represented by \(\mathsf{HybridResult}\), not declared to belong to \(\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\).

definitions.name: DCTFTR syntax, configurations, and terminals
definitions.construction:
Fix canonical finite orders on vertices, domains, descriptors, districts, assignments, complete response profiles, and generated work-DAG identifiers.  The counterfactual syntax is
\[
\mathsf{Atom}::=[s]V_\alpha=v,
\qquad
\mathsf{Event}::=\top\mid\bot\mid\mathsf{Atom}
\mid\mathsf{Event}\wedge\mathsf{Event}
\mid\mathsf{Event}\vee\mathsf{Event},
\]
where \(\alpha\) is a finite well-typed intervention or partial-copy term.  A descriptor declares a finite returned counterfactual tuple \(T_a\), a finite output alphabet \(\mathcal Y_a\), and a deterministic map \(f_a\).  Its output cell is the event \(\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\); the parser uses the pointwise preimage identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\}
\tag{1}
\]
only for normalization, locality tables, and response-profile evaluation.  The expression leaf for this cell is the directly supplied number \(P_a^s(y)\), not a collection of unsupplied tuple-cell probabilities.  Normalized events are canonical disjoint normal forms of consistent unnested atoms, including contradiction and sure-event forms.

Identified expressions have grammar
\[
\mathsf{Expr}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j
\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\nu_H),
\]
where \(J\) is finite, \(r\in\mathbb Q\), and \(\nu_H\) is an independently checked nonzero certificate on the declared fiber.  The phase-indexed work-node grammar is
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{Goal}::={}&
\operatorname{Raw}(\tau,e)
\mid\operatorname{Normed}(\tau,e,\nu)
\mid\operatorname{AncClosed}(\tau,H,e,\alpha)
\mid\operatorname{NeedRows}(\tau,D,C,b,\ell)\\
&\mid\operatorname{NeedFace}(\tau,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)
\mid\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})
\mid\operatorname{Prod}(\mathrm{children})
\mid\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta),
\end{split}
\]
with \(\tau\in\{\mathrm{num},\mathrm{den}\}\) and an accepting locality trace \(\ell\) on every row-needed node.  A configuration \(\mathsf{Config}\) is a finite well-typed acyclic DAG of these nodes, two distinguished roots, and a checked transition trace.

For \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), raw, normalized, and ancestor-closed nodes denote their target-domain event probabilities.  A row or face node at \((D,b)\) denotes \(b^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star(\mathbf M)\), a resolved node denotes \(F(\mathcal P)\), and sum and product nodes denote the finite sum and product of their children.  Configuration denotation is the ordered pair of root denotations.  Normalization derivations check consistency, unnesting, \((1)\), and finite disjoint Boolean identities pointwise.  Ancestor derivations enumerate every marginalized assignment.  Split derivations expand over the original districts \(\mathcal D(G)\), never over districts newly formed in an induced subgraph.  Extraction derivations are finite \(\mathsf{XEvent}\)- and \(\mathsf{XExpr}\)-trees with exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) tables, separate numerator and context rows, and independent positivity certificates; they contain no semantic row equality.  A face node is well typed only after literal verification of every equation in \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\).  Its row-space and forced-zero certificates use exact rational or real-algebraic linear arithmetic.  Zero, nonzero, and strict-positivity certificates are independently checked rational identities, exact linear certificates, or displayed finite preordering identities; none may consist of the conclusion it certifies.

The terminals are
\[
\mathsf{Result}::=
\operatorname{ID}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)
\mid\operatorname{FAIL}(t).
\]
Failure traces include ill-typed normalization or deterministic-preimage parsing, undefined original-district splitting, failed locality or extraction, \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\), \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}\), and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\).  For a nonterminal configuration define
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}
=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_\Sigma,r_\Pi,r_C)\in\mathbb N^8,
\]
counting respectively raw, normalized, ancestor-closed, row-needed, face-needed, unresolved-sum, unresolved-product nodes, and one terminalization flag; every terminal has rank zero.

definitions.name: Cross-menu face-preservation handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{preserve}}\) starts from the exact feasible face \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) and tracks both its affine hull and forced-zero coordinates through ancestor restriction, fixing, district splitting, and marginalization in \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\).

definitions.name: Layer-3 menu-acquisition handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{acquire}}\) enumerates realizable regime blocks \((R_e,p_e)\), propagates each full dependent block through the finite dual bases defining arm values on \(\mathcal K_S\), and solves the finite ex-post covering problem \(\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\) subject to \(\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).

definitions.name: Partial-district invariance-frontier handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{leak}}\) splits a selected district response kernel across \(D\cap\Delta_s\) and \(D\setminus\Delta_s\), tests whether supplied and target Layer-3 factors depend on a common invariant marginal kernel, and searches the smallest binary crossing perturbation when they do not.

definitions.name: Exact saturated response-profile and sparse canonical fibers
definitions.construction:
Use the complete query-independent carriers \(\Omega_D=\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\).  For \(\theta=(q_D^s:s\in\mathcal S,D\in\mathcal D(G))\), define
\[
\Psi_C^s(\theta^s)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1\{C\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }\omega\}
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^s(\omega_D).
\tag{1}
\]
If the indicator visits \(k\) districts, \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district-law blocks and has total degree at most \(k\).  For descriptor \(a\) and output \(y\in\mathcal Y_a\), let
\[
C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\]
Its indicator in \((1)\) is evaluated by the finite deterministic preimage, while its menu value is directly \(P_a^s(y)\).  Define
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\theta:{}&
q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)
\quad(s\in\mathcal S,D\in\mathcal D(G)),\\
&q_D^s=q_D^\star
\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Psi_{C_{a,y}}^s(\theta^s)=P_a^s(y)
\quad\text{for every }s,a,y\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\tag{2}
\]
For a target cell \(T\), set
\[
L_T(\mathcal P)=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\qquad
U_T(\mathcal P)=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\]
and
\[
\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)=
\Psi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)
-\Psi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star).
\]

For an arbitrary, possibly nonsaturated ADMG \(G\), let \(\vartheta^s=(\mu^s,p^s)\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\).  Its canonical coordinates satisfy
\[
p_U^s(u)\geq0,\quad\sum_up_U^s(u)=1,
\quad \mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s\in\{0,1\},
\quad \sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V}\mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s=1,
\]
together with every graph-compatible within-district latent-factor restriction and independence across original districts.  Let \(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)\) be the polynomial obtained by finite recursive evaluation and let \(q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)\) be the induced complete district response law.  Define
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\vartheta:{}&
\vartheta^s\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)
\quad(s\in\mathcal S),\\
&q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)
=q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\cdot;\vartheta^\star)
\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Phi_{C_{a,y},\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)=P_a^s(y)
\quad\text{for every complete supplied output cell}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\tag{3}
\]
Every occurrence of \(\mathcal P\) in \((2)\)--\((3)\) denotes the current complete typed-menu argument, whether it is the base menu or a finite complete-menu augmentation.  Every newly disclosed output cell, including every complementary cell of its finite output law, is imposed simultaneously; no base-menu equation and no complete cell rejected by a local row checker is discarded.  Neither fiber definition presupposes positivity of an evidence event.  The fiber in \((2)\) has district-saturated response-block semantics.  The fiber in \((3)\) retains all internal graph-compatible restrictions of the sparse ADMG.

definitions.name: Saturated typed-menu compatibility fiber
definitions.construction:
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}).
\]

definitions.name: District-separated complete-menu condition
definitions.construction: For \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds when every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain satisfying \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) has, under recursive evaluation on \(\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_{D'}\), an indicator that is either independent of \(\omega_D\), or depends only on \(\omega_D\).  In the second case its raw row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}\) and value \(P_a^s(v)\) must occur in \((A_D,m_D)\).  This is a finite syntactic and tabular condition; it excludes an unrecorded cross-district polynomial constraint involving \(q_D^\star\).

definitions.name: District-saturated response-block transport subclass
definitions.construction:
Define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete for every }D\in\mathcal D(G);\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ and }D\in\mathcal D(G),
\text{ exactly one finite latent block }U_D^s\text{ taking values in }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{stores one full deterministic response map for every vertex in }D
\text{ at every parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation in }D\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&(U_D^s:D\in\mathcal D(G))\text{ are mutually independent within each domain }s;\\
&\text{the class contains every independent choice of one probability law on }
\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ for each permitted district block},\\
&\text{subject only to equality of the laws of }U_D^s\text{ and }U_D^\star
\text{ whenever }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
Thus changed districts may use arbitrary and mutually unrelated response-block laws, unchanged districts use exactly the target response-block law, and no equality with the broad sparse-ADMG class \(\mathfrak M\) is asserted.

definitions.name: Focal-district-saturated response-block transport subclass and fiber
definitions.construction:
For a fixed district \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete};\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ there is exactly one finite latent block }
U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{storing one full deterministic response map for each vertex in }D
\text{ at every allowed parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation of a vertex in }D
\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&U_D^s\text{ is independent of the exogenous blocks of every }D'\ne D;\\
&\text{every probability law on }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ is permitted for }U_D^s,
\text{ subject only to equality with the target law}\\
&\text{when }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing;\\
&\text{for each }D'\ne D\text{, all structural tables, latent-factor restrictions,}
\text{ and cross-domain equalities remain those of }\mathfrak M
\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The phrase ``every probability law is permitted'' includes closure under replacing the law of \(U_D^\star\) and all its unchanged-source copies while holding all mechanisms and latent laws in districts \(D'\ne D\), and all changed-source copies of \(U_D\), fixed. Define
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
\]
and
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]

definitions.name: Active-slice face-separation condition
definitions.construction:
For a fixed district \(D\), define its active row space by
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+
\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}
\subseteq\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
For a complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), and for
\(\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'}\), define its focal recursive-indicator slice by
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}(\omega_D)
=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D.
\]
The active-slice face-separation predicate \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell and every fixed nonfocal response profile \(\omega_{-D}\).  When \(D\) is the only district, the nonfocal product is the singleton empty profile.

definitions.name: Baseline-averaged active-slice separation
definitions.construction:
Fix \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\).  For a baseline \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\), let
\[
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
=\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}q_{D'}^{0,s}(\omega_{D'}),
\qquad
\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'},
\]
where \(q_{D'}^{0,s}\) is the response-profile law induced by \(M^{0,s}\).  For every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), define the baseline-averaged focal row
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}
=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}
\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
The baseline-averaged active-slice predicate \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when there exists one \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) such that
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell.  The same witnessing baseline must be used for all cells and all feasible replacements of the focal law; a baseline depending on the replacement law is not permitted.

definitions.name: Finite constructive extraction calculus
definitions.construction:
The finite extraction calculus has event syntax
\[
\mathsf{XEvent}::=
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)\mid\top\mid\bot\mid
\neg\mathsf{XEvent}\mid
\bigsqcup_{j\in J}\mathsf{XEvent}_j\mid
\operatorname{Marg}_{W}(\mathsf{XEvent})\mid
\operatorname{Fix}(\mathsf{FixTrace},\mathsf{XEvent}),
\]
where \(J\) and every marginalized alphabet are finite, and a disjoint-union node carries a complete pointwise disjointness table.  The cell event is
\[
\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,y)=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}.
\]
Its probability leaf is the supplied output cell \(P_a^s(y)\).  Only its recursively evaluated indicator is expanded by the finite identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{f_a(T_a)=y\}
=\sum_{t:f_a(t)=y}\mathbf 1\{T_a=t\};
\tag{1}
\]
the tuple-cell probabilities on the right of \((1)\) are not menu generators unless an identity-output tuple descriptor is separately supplied.

Menu expressions have syntax
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{XExpr}::={}&
\operatorname{CellProb}(s,a,y)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)
\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j
\mid\mathsf{XExpr}-\mathsf{XExpr}
\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{XExpr}_j\\
&\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,H,\pi_H),
\end{split}
\]
where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(\pi_H\) is a separately checkable strict-positivity certificate on its declared compatibility fiber.  A derivation \(\delta:A\Downarrow F\) is generated only by an output-cell lookup, the truth-table identity \((1)\), contradiction or sure-event evaluation, finite disjoint additivity, complementation, finite marginalization, multiplication of independent original-district factors, and a checked fixing trace.

A fixing trace is a finite tree whose leaves are event or expression derivations and whose constructors are identity, typed substitution from a fixed finite registry of sound Boolean or fixing identities, finite disjoint sum, finite product, complement, marginalization, conditional quotient with a separately checked positive denominator, composition, and cleared-denominator comparison.  Every constructor stores all of its children and type data.  A comparison node is accepted only when cross-multiplication is legal under its stored denominator certificates and coefficient-by-coefficient normalization gives the zero polynomial.  The identity registry is finite and contains only pointwise Boolean identities, finite total-probability identities, and the fixing identities explicitly verified by recursive substitution of structural response tables.  Thus no constructor contains the semantic equality it is intended to establish.

Positivity certificates are either a positive rational constant after exact normalization, a rational Farkas identity for a linear face, or a displayed finite preordering identity
\[
p-\varepsilon=
\sum_i\tau_i h_i+
\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}}\sigma_J
\prod_{j\in J}g_j,
\qquad \varepsilon>0,
\]
where the declared fiber has equations \(h_i=0\), inequalities \(g_j\geq0\), and every \(\sigma_J\) is checked coefficient by coefficient to be a finite sum of squares.  All polynomial equalities are checked by exact integer or rational coefficient comparison.

For an event \(A\) and a district \(D\), the total procedure \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(A)\) enumerates
\[
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\longmapsto
\mathbf 1\{A\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\}
\]
over the complete finite response carriers.  It accepts exactly when every two entries with the same \(\omega_D\) agree, and then returns their common row \(\operatorname{row}_D(A)\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\).  Otherwise it returns the first disagreeing pair in the canonical order.  All syntax trees, registries, coefficient vectors, truth tables, and searches are finite and canonically ordered.

definitions.name: Source-labelled lossless stacked district system
definitions.construction:
Fix \(D\).  Enumerate every domain, descriptor, complete output cell, and extraction record canonically.  A candidate is transport admissible only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  First retain every admissible complete output cell \(C_{a,y}=\{f_a(T_a)=y\}\) whose exhaustive \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D\) table accepts, with row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y}\) and supplied value \(P_a^s(y)\).  Next, for every successful extraction judgment retain separately the numerator pair
\[
(r_{s,a,D,h,c},N_{s,a,D,h,c})
\]
and the context pair
\[
(v_{s,a,D,h},H_{s,a,D,h}).
\]
Never stack the quotient \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\) as a linear row.  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\) with value one and stack precisely the accepted raw, numerator, and context rows as \(A_D\), with their values in the same order as \(m_D\).  A failed locality, fixing, expression, positivity, or admissibility check contributes no row.  A rejected complete cell remains, without information loss, among the complete polynomial equalities of the exact global fiber.  For a deterministic postprocessor, recursive locality and the raw incidence row use the preimage identity \((1)\) from \(\mathrm{def:finite\text{-}extraction\text{-}calculus}\), but the stacked value is the directly supplied output probability \(P_a^s(y)\).

definitions.name: District-closed Layer-3 transport recursion
definitions.construction:
Initialize a finite acyclic work DAG with roots \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{num},B_\rho\cap E)\) and \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{den},E)\).  The deterministic priority rules are \(\mathsf{NORM}\), \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\), \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\), \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\), \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\), \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\), \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\), and \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\), using the rank from \(\mathrm{def:dctftr\text{-}grammar}\) and least-node tie breaking.

The normalization rule expands deterministic output cells only through the pointwise preimage identity and checks Boolean equality.  The ancestor rule records its complete finite marginalization identity.  At split, run \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(C)\) for every original district in canonical order.  An accepting trace creates \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(\tau,D,C,b,\ell)\).  If no original district is local, splice the exact original-district expansion
\[
P_{M^\star}(C)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1_C(\omega)
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^\star(\omega_D)
\tag{1}
\]
as a finite sum-product DAG.  No factorization over districts newly formed by an induced subgraph is used.  An enumeration or typing failure returns its typed split failure.

At extraction, enumerate every domain, descriptor, complete supplied output cell, and constructive extraction record.  Retain a candidate only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  Retain a raw output-cell row only when its exhaustive locality table accepts, and retain every derived numerator and context row separately.  Never retain a conditional quotient as a row.  Prepend normalization, construct \((A_D,m_D)\) exactly as in \(\mathrm{def:stacked\text{-}menu\text{-}system}\), and replay the derivations to check each equality in \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\) literally.  Rejected candidates are recorded and remain constraints of the global canonical fiber.

At face identification, compute the forced-zero set by exact linear programming and accept only a checked representation
\[
b_D=\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_D+
\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega.
\tag{2}
\]
It then resolves the node to \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}m_D\).  Failure of membership returns \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\), whose witness concerns only the local row relaxation; when only normalization survives, the same failed face test is labelled \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\).  Ready sum and product rules use finite additivity and the original-district factorization in \((1)\).

Condition returns uniform zero evidence only with an independent certificate, divides only with an independent certificate of strict positivity throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), returns a displayed compatible zero-evidence model when available, and otherwise returns uncertified positivity.  In priority order, the first seven rules decrease respectively \(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_\Sigma,r_\Pi\), fix every earlier coordinate, and create no earlier-phase node; condition decreases \(r_C\) only after the other coordinates vanish.  Every partial operation has its stated failure branch, so \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable from a well-typed initial configuration.

definitions.name: Real-semantic quantifier-elimination hybrid terminal grammar
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathbb D\) be the effective ordered coefficient ring generated by the finitely many supplied rational or real-algebraic output-cell probabilities.  Their stipulated effective presentations give exact arithmetic and sign comparison in \(\mathbb D\), and an order-preserving embedding \(\mathbb D\hookrightarrow\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) supplies exact coefficient representations.  A \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) is finite syntax for a quantifier-free Boolean combination of polynomial sign tests with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\).  For every real-closed field \(K\) containing an ordered copy of \(\mathbb D\), this syntax has the usual realization \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_K\) in its displayed free variables.  In particular, the causal realization used below is \(\llbracket\chi\rrbracket_{\mathbb R}\) over the ordinary real field; neither canonical probability variables nor free target-value variables are restricted to \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).

The hybrid terminal grammar is exactly
\[
\begin{split}
\mathsf{HybridResult}::={}&
\operatorname{ID\_RAT}(F,\delta)
\mid\operatorname{UNCOND\_QE}(\chi_T,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton})\\
&\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE\_QE}
\mid\operatorname{NOT\_UNIFORMLY\_DEFINED\_QE}\\
&\mid\operatorname{COND\_QE}(\chi_Q,\chi_{\min},\chi_{\max},\mathsf{isSingleton}),
\end{split}
\tag{1}
\]
where each displayed \(\chi\) is a \(\mathsf{QEFormula}\) and \(\mathsf{isSingleton}\) is the exact Boolean output of the associated closed first-order sentence.

The deterministic procedure \(\mathsf{DCTFTR\text{-}CAN}\) first runs \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\).  A successful rational identification is returned as \(\operatorname{ID\_RAT}\).  Every other terminal invokes the graph-compatible canonical fiber
\[
S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P).
\]
Every quantifier-elimination call below is made in the first-order language of real-closed fields with coefficients in \(\mathbb D\); its computation performs only exact coefficient operations in \(\mathbb D\), and its returned syntax is interpreted over \(\mathbb R\).  For \(p_T=\Phi_{T,\mathrm{can}}^\star\), apply quantifier elimination to
\[
\varphi_T(t):=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge t-p_T(x)=0]
\tag{2}
\]
and denote the output by \(\chi_T(t)\).  Apply it to the closed sentence
\[
\exists t_1,t_2\,[\chi_T(t_1)\wedge\chi_T(t_2)\wedge t_1\ne t_2]
\tag{3}
\]
and to
\[
\chi_T(\ell)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow\ell\leq t],
\qquad
\chi_T(u)\wedge\forall t\,[\chi_T(t)\Longrightarrow t\leq u]
\tag{4}
\]
to form the singleton Boolean and endpoint formulas.

For a conditional target put \(e=\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star\) and \(n=\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E,\mathrm{can}}^\star\).  Define
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathsf Z:&\neg\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0],\\
\mathsf N:&\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)=0]
\ \wedge\ \exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0],\\
\mathsf P:&\neg\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)=0].
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
Three quantifier-elimination calls yield closed quantifier-free formulas whose exact constant sign evaluations decide \(\mathsf Z\), \(\mathsf N\), and \(\mathsf P\).  On any explicitly supplied nonempty canonical fiber, the single closed formula in \(\mathsf P\) is the reusable uniform-positivity decision; the full block in \((5)\) is used when a failed positivity screen must be classified as uniform zero or mixed zero and positive evidence.  The zero, mixed, and positive meanings and the two payload-free terminal labels are unchanged after replacing \(S\) consistently throughout the block.  The first two cases return the corresponding payload-free evidence terminals.  Only in case \(\mathsf P\) is quantifier elimination applied to
\[
\varphi_Q(t):=\exists x\,[x\in S\wedge e(x)>0\wedge e(x)t-n(x)=0]
\tag{6}
\]
to form \(\chi_Q(t)\), its singleton Boolean, and endpoint formulas as in \((3)\)--\((4)\).  The procedure returns formulas and decisions only: it returns no explicit endpoint value, algebraic sample, cylindrical algebraic decomposition trace, canonical parameter, or paired SCM.

definitions.name: Exact subset-fiber evidence positivity
definitions.construction:
For every \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define
\[
\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\neg\exists\vartheta\,
\left[\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\ \wedge\
\Phi_{E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star)=0\right].
\]
The predicate is used only when \(\Lambda_S\ne\varnothing\), and its displayed
closed real formula is evaluated by the exact quantifier-elimination semantics of
\(\mathrm{def:hybrid\text{-}result\text{-}grammar}\).

definitions.name: Exact global sparse-ADMG regime-block acquisition
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathcal U\) be a finite set of physically realizable candidate experiments.  Each \(e\in\mathcal U\) discloses a finite block of complete typed output laws, including every cell of each declared finite output, whose probabilities are effectively rational or real algebraic, and has an effectively comparable cost \(c_e>0\).  For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), let \(\mathcal P_S\) be \(\mathcal P\) augmented by all complete output laws disclosed by experiments in \(S\), and define
\[
\Lambda_S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P_S).
\]
An admissible global acquisition instance is required to satisfy \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\ne\varnothing\).  For every \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), use \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\) from \(\mathrm{def:global\text{-}subset\text{-}positivity}\).

Apply the closed zero, mixed, and positive evidence tests of \(\mathrm{def:hybrid\text{-}result\text{-}grammar}\) to the full fiber \(\Lambda_{\mathcal U}\).  Uniform zero evidence or mixed zero and positive evidence returns the corresponding payload-free status and leaves the numerical full-menu conditional arm-ranking benchmark undefined.  Only when \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(\mathcal U)\) holds define
\[
n_\rho(\vartheta)
=\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star).
\]
For a subset \(S\), define its numerical possibly-optimal set only when \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\) holds, by
\[
\operatorname{PO}_G(S)
=\left\{\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}:
\exists\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ 
n_\rho(\vartheta)-n_\sigma(\vartheta)\geq0\right\}.
\]
Set
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full},G}=\operatorname{PO}_G(\mathcal U),
\qquad
f_G(S)=|\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}|-|\operatorname{PO}_G(S)|
\]
on positive subsets, and define the exact broad-model ex-post acquisition problem by
\[
\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{PO}_G(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full},G}.
\]
Thus the acquired full menu, rather than the unaugmented menu, is required to establish uniform conditional definability.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\).  For every retained \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\),
\[
N_{s,a,D,h,c}=r_{s,a,D,h,c}^{\mathsf T}q_D^s,
\qquad
H_{s,a,D,h}=v_{s,a,D,h}^{\mathsf T}q_D^s>0,
\]
and therefore
\[
K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=
\frac{r_{s,a,D,h,c}^{\mathsf T}q_D^s}
{v_{s,a,D,h}^{\mathsf T}q_D^s}.
\]
Only after a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) may \(q_D^s\) be replaced by \(q_D^\star\).  Every accepted raw supplied output cell satisfies \(P_a^s(y)=(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,y})^{\mathsf T}q_D^s\), with the same admissibility requirement for transport.  A \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record gives the target numerator and evidence equations \(P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\cap E)=n_{\rho,D}^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star\) and \(P_{M^\star}(E)=d_D^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star\); an accepted generic target locality trace gives \(P_{M^\star}(C)=b_D^{\mathsf T}q_D^\star\).  Every rejected extraction, locality, positivity, or admissibility check contributes no row.
statements.justification: This converts every heterogeneous Layer-3 input and each target arm comparison into exact linear information on a fixed response carrier.
statements.gap: Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim give canonical response carriers, while CTFIDU+ extracts Layer-3 factors; neither gives a source-labelled common-evidence row system under district-level transport.
statements.consumer: The row representation supplies the primal and dual programs used by the face-aware identification and arm-ordering certificates.

statements.statement:
For every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Suppose \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds.  This predicate entails \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), and
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Moreover,
\[
R_D(m_D)
=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp}.
\]
For the single witnessing baseline \(\mathbf M^0\) in \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), every transport-admissible complete supplied cell is preserved under replacement of its focal law \(q_0\) by an arbitrary \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) because
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}(q-q_0)=0.
\]
Every boundary point of the row face is therefore induced on the declared alphabets \(\mathcal X\) by a compatible SCM family saturated only at \(D\), while every district \(D'\ne D\) retains its original graph-compatible restrictions.  Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence also together with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is a convenient sufficient condition for \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\).  Without baseline-averaged separation or focal-district saturation, only the displayed broad inclusion is asserted.
statements.justification: The equality is the causal realization step making focal-district optimization sharp whenever one compatible baseline preserves all complete-menu cells through their averaged focal rows.
statements.gap: Existing Layer-3 completeness results do not give this heterogeneous fixed-alphabet projection theorem or isolate the weaker baseline-averaged condition from pointwise slice separation.
statements.consumer: Every local optimizer becomes an explicit compatible SCM while all nonfocal districts retain their graph-compatible baseline restrictions.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\operatorname{SupportLocal}_D(C)\) accepts and constructs \(b_D=\operatorname{row}_D(C)\).  For the broad compatibility fiber, membership in
\[
b_D\in R_D(m_D)
=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+
\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}
\]
is sufficient to identify the causal target \(P_{M^\star}(C)\), with explicit value \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}m_D\) whenever
\[
b_D=\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_D+
\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega.
\]
If additionally \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, membership is necessary for constancy on \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\).  On that focal-district-saturated baseline-averaged class, failure yields two original-alphabet compatible SCM families with identical supplied laws and unequal target-cell probabilities while every \(D'\ne D\) retains its baseline graph-compatible restrictions.  Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is sufficient for this exact clause.  If target locality rejects, or outside the baseline-averaged focal-projection scope, no such local converse is asserted.
statements.justification: Forced-zero coordinates give broad identification and, under exact single-baseline focal projection, a necessary fixed-alphabet criterion with paired countermodels.
statements.gap: Published Layer-3 identification does not provide this boundary-face row-space characterization or the weaker baseline-averaged source-labelled realization condition.
statements.consumer: Menus that preserve cross-district cells only after averaging under a compatible baseline can identify targets and certify nonidentification beyond pointwise slice tests.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), each nonterminal \(\mathsf{NORM}\), \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\), \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\), \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\), \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\), \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\), or \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\) step preserves the ordered pair of root denotations pointwise. The preservation witnesses are respectively the checked normalization derivation, finite ancestor marginalization identity, checked district sum-product derivation, admissible extraction equations \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\), active-face calculation, finite additivity, and district factorization. The \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) rule labels its terminal with the same two root values and divides only under an independent strict-positivity certificate. In the rank \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\), the first seven rules respectively decrease \(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi}\) while fixing every earlier coordinate, and \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) decreases \(r_C\) after the others vanish; no rule creates an earlier-phase node. The fixed priority and least-applicable-node convention give a unique successor. From a well-typed initial configuration, \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable because every declared partial-operation failure takes its specified \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) branch.
statements.justification: A typed operational semantics needs a local invariant for every transition before terminal soundness follows.
statements.gap: The prior transport recursions prove their own rule systems sound, but do not cover certified Layer-3 extraction from heterogeneous source-labelled laws.
statements.consumer: The local invariant supports independent checking of a returned derivation or failure trace.

statements.statement: For every realizable typed menu with \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), the priority transition system \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) has a unique finite run because \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}\in\mathbb N^8\) decreases lexicographically. Every reached configuration has root denotation \((P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\wedge E),P_{M^\star}(E))\) for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). If the result is \(\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi)\), then \(F_B,F_E\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\), \(\pi\) proves \(F_E>0\) throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), and \(F_B(\mathcal P)/F_E(\mathcal P)=Q_\rho^\star(\mathbf M)\) for every compatible model. If \(z\) proves \(F_E=0\) throughout the fiber, the result is \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) and the conditional is undefined. A split failure, failed extraction, normalization-only face failure, denominator witness at zero, or uncertified denominator positivity returns its typed \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) trace and performs no division. A \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\) witness certifies only local district-face variation and implies global nonidentification only when the hypotheses of the one-district fiber-projection theorem are separately verified. The observed numerical sign of \(F_E\) is never itself a positivity certificate, and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable from a well-typed initial configuration.
statements.justification: The source-labelled Layer-3 recursion must be valid before its output can enter the sharper arm-ordering analysis.
statements.gap: CTFTR handles heterogeneous Layer-1/2 inputs and CTFIDU+ handles one-specification Layer-3 inputs; neither soundness argument covers both features simultaneously.
statements.consumer: A successful output can be evaluated directly from released source tables, while impossible conditioning events are rejected before division.

statements.statement: Under the finite semi-Markovian convention, the observational and atomic hard-interventional restriction \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFTR}}\) has a proper typed embedding into \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{DCTFTR}}\). The DCTFTR-expressible intersection \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFIDU+}}\) of the published one-SCM Layer-3 grammar has a proper typed embedding obtained by setting \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\) and applying its declared constructor map. No embedding of the full CTFTR conditional or stochastic-policy grammar, and no embedding of an undeclared CTFIDU+ Layer-2.5 action, is asserted. On either embedded restriction, every successful DCTFTR functional and every successful functional returned by the corresponding published calculus equals the same causal query in every compatible model; syntactic or transition-by-transition equivalence is not asserted. In \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the first restriction cannot accept the genuine cross-world cell \(p\), while the complete source-labelled family with \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\) is not realizable by one SCM and hence is outside the second restriction.
statements.justification: Typed proper embeddings state exactly which published input classes are recovered and where the multi-domain Layer-3 language is strictly larger.
statements.gap: CTFTR and CTFIDU+ occupy different proper subgrammars; neither accepts the complete binary multi-domain instance.
statements.consumer: Users can recognize settled CTFTR and CTFIDU+ cases while reserving DCTFTR for genuinely heterogeneous Layer-3 inputs.

statements.statement:
Suppose a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record is given and \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\).  Then
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=
\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}}
\{m_D^{\mathsf T}\eta:A_D^{\mathsf T}\eta
\leq g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\}.
\]
Every feasible dual vector with \(m_D^{\mathsf T}\eta>0\) certifies \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) in every model in the broad fiber \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  If additionally \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, a positive dual value is also necessary for uniform strict dominance on \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\).  Under that hypothesis, \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0\) is attained by an original-alphabet focal-district-saturated SCM with the reverse strict ranking, and
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0<
\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)
\]
yields two such same-menu SCM families with opposite rankings while preserving every nonfocal district.  Nonemptiness of the focal fiber together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D\), is sufficient for the exact clauses.  Without the total checked-local-arms record the conditional comparison is undefined; without baseline-averaged focal projection, primal optimizers need not lift.
statements.justification: The theorem gives an auditable broad-fiber dual certificate and exact opposing focal SCMs under the sharp single-baseline projection condition.
statements.gap: Transported bandit results do not derive this heterogeneous Layer-3 dual certificate or baseline-averaged fixed-alphabet countermodel lift.
statements.consumer: A bandit analyst can audit strict removal by source-table weights and lift a reversing optimizer without altering any nonfocal district.

statements.statement: Suppose a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record is given and \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\).  For every realizable additional complete output-cell row \(r_D^\dagger\), \(I_D\) is a closed interval and \(p\mapsto\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\) is a finite convex piecewise-affine function.  Its pieces are obtained from feasible bases of the row-augmented dual and have coefficients rational affine in \(m_D\).  Consequently \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\) is the complement in \(I_D\) of a closed convex subset, which is empty, a point, or a closed interval, and has zero, one, or two relative sign boundaries.  Every boundary has a zero-valued dual menu certificate and a primal row-face law attaining equality; every adjacent strict-pruning side has a positive dual piece.  If the augmented menu at a boundary satisfies \(\mathsf{BASep}_D\), the equality law is realized by an original-alphabet SCM saturated only at \(D\), with every nonfocal district unchanged.  Nonemptiness of the augmented focal fiber together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D\), is sufficient for this realization.  Without the checked-local-arms record the frontier is undefined; without baseline-averaged focal projection, no causal lifting of a row-face boundary is asserted.
statements.justification: This gives the exact parametric Layer-3 sign boundary and realizes boundary laws under the augmented menu's sharp single-baseline condition.
statements.gap: Existing fixed-menu and bandit results do not give a parametric Layer-3 cell diagram with baseline-averaged focal boundary SCMs.
statements.consumer: A study designer can locate pruning regions and obtain a boundary SCM whenever one compatible baseline preserves the augmented menu.

statements.statement: For \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the base face has the unique parameterization \(q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p)\), \(0\le p\le1/2\), and \[Q_\rho(q(p))=1-2p,\qquad Q_\sigma(q(p))=1/2,\qquad I_D=[0,1/2],\qquad \Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)=2p-1/2,\qquad \mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+=(1/4,1/2].\] With the augmented row order consisting of the three rows of \(A_D\) followed by \(r_D^\dagger\), the dual vector \((0,-1,0,2)^\top\) represents \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) exactly and has value \(2p-1/2\); at the realized value \(p=3/8\) it certifies margin \(1/4\). The boundary SCM is \(q(1/4)=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4)\), while \(q(0)\) makes \(\rho\) strictly optimal and \(q(1/2)\) makes \(\sigma\) strictly optimal on the original binary alphabets. For the sole unit-cost block, \[\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\{\rho,\sigma\},\qquad \mathcal K_{\{e^\dagger\}}=\{q(3/8)\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(\{e^\dagger\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.\] The first equality is witnessed by \(p=0\) for \(\rho\) and \(p=1/2\) for \(\sigma\); at \(p=3/8\), \(Q_\sigma=1/2>1/4=Q_\rho\), and no other arm exists because \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\).
statements.justification: This exhaustive binary calculation verifies the sign frontier, the dual certificate, the boundary law, and the decision consequence in one complete instance.
statements.gap: The published identification and bandit papers do not exhibit a heterogeneous genuine Layer-3 cell whose observed value crosses an exact transported pruning boundary.
statements.consumer: The instance is a regression test for extraction, face identification, experiment blocking, and undefined-arm-safe pruning.

statements.statement:
Suppose a \(\mathsf{CheckedLocalArms}_D\) record is given.  If there exists \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) with
\[
A_D^{\mathsf T}\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}
\leq g_{\rho,\sigma,D},
\qquad
m_D^{\mathsf T}\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}>0,
\]
then removing \(\rho\) cannot remove a maximizing arm from \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\).  A candidate comparison for which the common-evidence checker instead certifies uniform zero is excluded as undefined rather than ranked.
statements.justification: This records the elementary decision consequence while keeping it out of the research kernel.
statements.gap: The exclusion rule itself is elementary and is not positioned as a strengthening of Park and Lee; the new content is the derived sharp certificate in Theorems 5 and 6.
statements.consumer: A counterfactual bandit can initialize exploration on the certificate-retained action set without treating undefined conditionals as low rewards.

statements.statement: Can \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{preserve}}\) be completed into a multi-district theorem that projects the full source-labelled compatibility fiber onto the exact product-constrained faces needed for \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\), so that every failed arm-order certificate yields two original-alphabet SCM families with opposite ranking, or does the smallest binary two-hedge thicket contain a recursive failure whose target score is already constant on the global fiber?
statements.justification: This is the genuine open local-to-global step; the boundary-face correction must survive nonlinear district gluing before global completeness can be claimed.
statements.gap: CTFIDU+ combines failed factors with independent bit coordinates, while CTFTR proves Layer-1/2 graphical completeness; neither preserves active faces of heterogeneous Layer-3 menu fibers through multi-district recursion.
statements.consumer: A positive answer gives complete global ranking certificates, while a negative smallest thicket identifies the exact instance that requires sharp polynomial bounds instead.

statements.statement: For the finite ex-post problem \[\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\quad\text{subject to}\quad\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}},\] can \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{acquire}}\) characterize all minimum-cost regime-block solutions? In particular, is \(f(S)=\lvert\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\rvert-\lvert\operatorname{PO}(S)\rvert\) submodular, meaning that for every \(S\subseteq T_{\mathrm{exp}}\subseteq\mathcal U\) and \(e\notin T_{\mathrm{exp}}\), \[f(S\cup\{e\})-f(S)\ge f(T_{\mathrm{exp}}\cup\{e\})-f(T_{\mathrm{exp}}),\] or is there a finite realizable obstruction with an exact mixed-integer dual certificate?
statements.justification: The objective makes offline acquisition a finite ex-post design problem at the regime-block level, with a precise diminishing-returns question.
statements.gap: Raghavan and Bareinboim name counterfactual-intervention selection for tighter bounds as open, while Park and Lee enumerate actions but do not optimize which Layer-3 laws should be acquired for transported pruning.
statements.consumer: A platform with costly partial-copy experiments can choose the cheapest offline blocks reproducing the full-menu possibly-optimal set without conflating this choice with an adaptive policy.

statements.statement: Can district closure be replaced by a strictly weaker graph-checkable kernel-separability condition that is necessary and sufficient for transporting declared Layer-3 rows, with \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{leak}}\) producing an invariant reduction when it holds and an original-alphabet paired-SCM leakage certificate when it fails?
statements.justification: Whole-district selection is transparent but may be stronger than necessary for a particular Layer-3 factor.
statements.gap: Classical selection diagrams permit vertex-level shifts, but no located result characterizes which cross-world kernel remains invariant inside a partially selected district.
statements.consumer: Multi-site studies changing only one mechanism inside a confounded block could certify transport without declaring the whole district incomparable.

sampling_model.design: Exact population laws from finite source-labelled menus of observational, hard-interventional, and declared realizable partial-copy regimes.
sampling_model.units: Each law is generated by independent units from its domain-specific finite recursive SCM; identification is at the population-law level.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatments and partial-copy operations are fixed by descriptor \(a\), and source shifts are encoded by \(\Delta_s\).
sampling_model.overlap: No blanket positivity assumption is imposed. The recursion returns \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) for an identified zero evidence probability, and arm-order theorems explicitly restrict to a face on which the common evidence row is positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance estimator enters the identification claim; finite-sample estimation of returned functionals and dual margins is downstream.

estimand_functional: The exact broad conditional range is \(\left[\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)/\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),\ \max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)/\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)\right]\) when \(\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)>0\), for \((\Lambda,\Xi)\in\{(\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\}\).  The QE syntax is computed over the effective coefficient ring and interpreted over \(\mathbb R\).  For global acquisition, \(\Lambda_S=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P_S)\) and \(\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) is defined only when \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\), with \(\rho\in\operatorname{PO}_G(S)\) exactly when some \(\vartheta\in\Lambda_S\) satisfies \(n_\rho(\vartheta)\geq n_\sigma(\vartheta)\) for every \(\sigma\).  The numerical benchmark requires \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(\mathcal U)\), and the exact design minimizes \(\sum_{e\in S}c_e\) subject to \(\operatorname{Pos}_G(S)\) and \(\operatorname{PO}_G(S)=\operatorname{PO}_G(\mathcal U)\).  Locally, the checked base-face evidence lower bound makes every subset positive; \(R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp}\), and the LP dominance and acquisition maps are exact only under focal saturation plus \(\mathsf{BASep}_D\) or its stated stronger sufficient checks; otherwise they are outer relaxations of the broad canonical program.

tldr: Heterogeneous sites can supply genuine Layer-3 partial-copy laws. A certified extraction judgment turns each available context and cell into a typed district row only after source admissibility is proved. On a fixed-alphabet one-district compatibility face, the sharp transported arm-gap equals an explicit dual weighting of all retained source-labelled cells, and an added Layer-3 regime block yields a finite piecewise-affine pruning frontier. DCTFTR is an inductive, terminating transition system with typed failures and zero-evidence rejection. A complete binary instance gives the margin \(2p-1/2\), while minimum-cost regime-block acquisition and multi-district face preservation remain explicit open questions.

project_justification.gap: CTFTR transports conditional counterfactuals from heterogeneous Layer-1/2 inputs, CTFIDU+ identifies from Layer-3 inputs in one causal specification, and Park--Lee pruning uses graph-based action classes or fixed transported bounds. None derives an exact source-menu certificate or a sign-regime boundary for the order of conditional Layer-3 arms.
project_justification.niche: District-closed shifts and common-evidence arm comparisons reduce one confounded target block to a boundary-sensitive response polytope. Its LP dual converts released source cells into an auditable ranking certificate, while a candidate menu value parametrizes a genuine pruning phase transition.
project_justification.fill: The project proves fixed-alphabet realization of the compatible face, gives certified typed extraction and an inductive DCTFTR semantics, replaces global row span by an active-face criterion, derives sharp primal--dual arm-order certificates, verifies the complete binary phase boundary, and poses minimum-cost regime-block acquisition before asking whether the construction survives multi-district gluing.

related_work: Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (2022, Theorem 5.1) supply the source-labelled conditional transport architecture for Layers 1 and 2; Proposition 1 proves proper typed inclusion of their problem-instance subgrammar and sound semantic agreement of successful functionals, without asserting syntactic or transition-level equivalence. Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026, Theorem 3.5 and Appendix E.1) supply Layer-3 factor extraction and ctf-thickets for one causal specification; Proposition 1 embeds that setting through \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\) and proves non-representability of the complete binary multi-domain instance, without claiming that its scalar cell alone is outside CTFIDU+. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022, Theorem 2.4) supply the finite response carrier, and Choe et al. (2026, Proposition 3.1) motivate preserving all information rows; both inform rather than serve as tightening targets. Bareinboim and Pearl (2012, Theorems 5--7) and Bareinboim and Pearl (2014) supply vertex-level selection diagrams and multi-environment completeness, whereas district joint-kernel invariance is a stronger Layer-3 transport condition. Park and Lee (2026, ICLR, Theorems 1--3) define realizable Layer-3 action classes, and Park and Lee (2026, UAI, Theorems 1--2) give valid Layer-1/2 transported bandit bounds; they inform the menu-dual order certificate, binary pruning boundary, and ex-post block-acquisition question rather than serving as results claimed to be beaten.
technical_internal_limitation: Boundary fibers require the active normals \(e_\omega\) for \(\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\); ordinary row span alone can miss identification when the menu forces response profiles to zero. Multi-district completeness is not asserted. The smallest binary two-hedge thicket must compare every recursive failure with target-score constancy on the exact global compatibility fiber; a failed recursion with a constant target would redirect the global claim to sharp polynomial transported bounds.
honest_scope: The face projection, active-face identification criterion, dual arm-order theorem, one-cell phase diagram, and complete binary check concern a reduced one-district comparison with common positive evidence. DCTFTR soundness covers broader district-closed instances, but fixed-cardinality multi-district completeness is open. The acquisition objective is finite and ex post; it is not an ex-ante adaptive policy. No assumption supplies the dominance margin, active face, or threshold. The observational and hard-interventional problem-instance subgrammar is properly included in DCTFTR and successful outputs agree semantically with the target, the one-domain problem-instance class includes the CTFIDU+ setting, and sure evidence reduces conditional arm order to the unconditional numerator-gap program.
